Notes

Private worries become usable material, but the voice judging them tightens around the speaker like Sun Wukong’s headband.

脱口而出

脱口而出 means words coming straight out of the mouth before they are weighed or restrained. The line follows “I feel it,” making expression seem immediate. Soon he decides that too much expression will look self-pitying. The miniature story is already in that reversal: what arrives naturally acquires an imagined audience and becomes something to regulate.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
揭不开锅

揭不开锅 literally describes being unable to open the cooking pot, an idiom for having no food to cook. Calling such worries “potential wealth” turns deprivation into something a writer might use. The reversal is uncomfortable as well as resourceful: creative value does not fill the pot now, and naming it wealth can make the original need easy to overlook.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
矫情

矫情 here means affected, excessively dramatic or self-pitying. It is a judgment about the presentation of feeling, not proof that the feeling is false. The speaker imagines looking this way to other people before he has even explained much. The word lets a social criticism become an internal editor, deciding how much pain he is allowed to say aloud.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
幸福的守财奴

守财奴 is someone enslaved to guarding money—a miser, with 奴 carrying the word “slave.” Giving that figure happiness complicates the usual insult. He may possess what the speaker lacks, including the ease to judge somebody else’s worries. The line pits the earlier conversion of hardship into possible wealth against somebody already comfortably keeping hold of theirs.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
紧箍咒

In Journey to the West, Tang Sanzang can recite a spell that tightens Sun Wukong’s headband and forces him to obey through pain. 念叨, nagging or repeatedly talking at someone, leads directly into that image here: another person’s repeated voice becomes physical pressure. The title “Curse” therefore names both a familiar literary device and the experience of carrying that voice around.

  • Journey to the West, chapter 14
很重

The literary headband first constricts; this short line makes it heavy. Later the weight moves to the shoulders as a 担子, a load or responsibility. The recurring pressure migrates over the body, giving different kinds of obligation the same physical effect. Two ordinary words briefly interrupt the more elaborate imagery to make that effect plain.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
把酒言欢

把酒言欢 is polished, literary language for sharing a drink and talking happily. It follows the blunt “short fuse” and precedes a request to finish the performance. Good company may therefore be a role maintained while irritation remains underneath. The sequence compresses a familiar social task: keep the occasion agreeable until it is safe to leave.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
桃子放久了会变软

This homely observation arrives between maintaining a social performance and telling others to stay out of the relationship. Fruit changes when it is left too long; so do situations that are not addressed. The image adds time and fragility without spelling out a one-to-one metaphor. Its kitchen scale also recalls the pot and wealth at the song’s opening.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
往前走

The song gives forward motion two different pressures: a heavy burden pushes him on, and the order never to look back blocks retreat. Walking is not simply optimistic progress in this setting. It is the narrow option left when stopping and returning both feel unavailable. That shades the tape’s repeated “keep going” language with compulsion.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
洗不干净的手

The construction does not merely say the hands are dirty: washing fails to make them clean. That difference makes the stain feel persistent, something action cannot undo. The following refusal to turn back and confession to the air develop that persistence into a moral atmosphere. The song stays with the feeling of implication rather than specifying an act.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
对着空气自首

自首 is voluntarily turning oneself in, a word with an expected receiving authority. Confessing to empty air removes that listener, leaving the act suspended. The previous hands that will not wash clean give the gesture a sense of guilt without naming an offense. Speech happens, but it cannot obtain an answer, a judgment or release.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
别问我那么多问题

A song that began with feeling becoming speech ends by trying to stop a conversation. The questions themselves are something the speaker says he does not want to have. That folds curiosity back into pressure: being asked to explain can feel like another burden when he is still carrying the unresolved thing. The closing boundary does not supply a resolution.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
